summary: Closes §4.6 of docs/MYIDSAN_PRODUCTIZATION_PLAN.md ("Reverse-proxy guidance") with a documentation-only delivery -- no Go code changed. New deploy/reverse-proxy/ holds a working nginx-myidsan.conf (HTTP->HTTPS 308 redirect, TLS 1.2/1.3, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, no-cache on auth responses, and commented-out directives to disable upstream keep-alive for Kerberos SPNEGO) and an equivalent Caddyfile.myidsan, plus a README explaining the app-side half (enableTLS:false, nonTlsPorts, bind to loopback); why the public URL must not drift (registered redirect URIs match exactly, and a drifted URL fails every relying app at the callback, after the user already signed in); that X-Forwarded-* is a claim from the client, not a fact, so the proxy must overwrite rather than append it; setting rateLimit.trustedProxies so the audit trail and failed-login lockout key on the real client instead of the whole building; a warning not to set Caddy's trusted_proxies at the outermost edge (that makes Caddy start trusting inbound X-Forwarded-*, the opposite of an internet-facing hop); the Kerberos connection-affinity requirement (SPNEGO authenticates a connection, not a request); an air-gapped-TLS note; and a verification checklist. The plan also documents, with an explicit severity assessment, the known gap where middlewares.IsSecureRequest trusts X-Forwarded-Proto:https from any caller unlike ClientIP's trustedProxies allow-list: because the check is r.TLS!=nil || XFP==https, the header can only make a request look MORE secure, never less, so a genuine HTTPS request cannot be downgraded -- it only affects cookie-name/Secure-flag selection, making the exposure a self-inflicted denial of service (a caller asserting the header over cleartext gets Secure cookies its own browser then refuses to store), not privilege escalation or session fixation. The fix is deliberately deferred (five call sites across shared middleware, myidsan and myseliasan; it decides cookie naming suite-wide) and mitigated meanwhile by having the sample configs strip the header at the edge. deploy/README-myidsan.md, deploy/README.md (mymatasan), deploy/README-myseliasan.md, deploy/README-myiotsan.md, docs/TECHNICAL_SPEC.md, docs/HOWTO.md's Kerberos SPNEGO section, and the root README.md now cross-reference deploy/reverse-proxy/ from their existing TLS/rate-limit/trustedProxies mentions, since the X-Forwarded-*/trustedProxies trust model applies to all four apps even though the sample configs themselves are myidsan-specific.
compatibility: Documentation and sample-config addition only; no code, config schema, API, or runtime behavior changed for any app. Existing installs are entirely unaffected whether or not they adopt the reverse-proxy samples. The one code fix the plan flags (threading rateLimit.trustedProxies into middlewares.IsSecureRequest) is explicitly deferred, not shipped here.
